text:
A week ago, Stefan Noesen was in Utica. Then Anthony Mantha went on long-term injured reserve, New Jersey recalled Noesen and Lenni Hameenaho on Nov. 11, and the next night Noesen scored on a breakaway in a 5-2 win over Washington. The Devils won again in Washington two days later.

He's played only seven games, with 2 goals and 4 points in under ten minutes a night, so the rates mean nothing yet. What he brings is known: a hard right-handed shot (his hardest is in the top 3% of the league by speed), a willingness to go to the net, and 17 hits in those seven games. He isn't fast, with skating bursts near the bottom of the league, and last season was rough, around replacement level by Evolving-Hockey over a small sample.

The bigger story is his history with this team. The Plano, Texas native is on his second stint with the Devils, with Carolina in between. At 33, he's a depth forward filling a hole while Mantha is out. Whether he keeps the spot depends on how quickly the Devils get healthy.
